messages.author: f7958ed01e630103
messages.subject: resuming updating
parts: This may be a FAQ, but I did not find any discussion here.  In JAGS (specifically, rjags), if a model did not converge, we can use update() to resume sampling.  I read the description of stan() and was not sure if we can do the same, that is, resuming posterior sampling from where the model stopped, by specifying "fit=".  If not, is there a function similar to "update()" in rjags?  Thanks.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] resuming updating
parts:
No, there is no equivalent of rjags (or R2jags) updating
in RStan or Stan.

I posted a response about this recently, but the
list is so high-volume I can't even find it.

It would be nice to have, but our recommendation is to
just restart. Run 100 iterations, if that isn't enough,
run 200, and so on, until you get enough. At most you'll
have to do about twice as much work as you would by
restarting, but you get the benefit of adaptation running
longer each time.

The practical reason we haven't implemented it is saving
all the adaptation and RNG state. We have lots of adaptations
strategies, so there's not a standard way to do it, and the
Boost RNG we use do not support persistence. (And we want
results to be reproducible, at least within a given version of (R)Stan.)

- Bob

messages.author: 14cad522d99ed9fa
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] resuming updating
parts:
I have a somewhat related question. First, let's assume I know nothing about HMC/NUTS, and am using Stan simply because it is a shiny new tool (which isn't that far from the truth...).

I have a model whose MCMC has a dimension changing reversible jump step (with which I assume Stan would have difficulty). Currently, I run the RJ step every K iterations of MCMC (usually about 10-100), and use MH sampling (implemented in Rcpp) for everything else. It's very slow to converge, something I was hoping Stan might remedy. Thus I was thinking of doing this:

1. Run Stan for K iterations
2. Outside of Stan, do the RJ step
3. Run Stan for another K iterations, initializing the parameters at the values where the previous Stan run ended
4. Repeat 2 and 3 until convergence

Now, for my questions. Is this a good idea for HMC in general? Stan in particular?
Given Bob's previous response, and assuming this is reasonable in HMC, how should I approach this? Run with standard HMC instead of NUTS? (NUTS is where the adaptation occurs, correct?)

Sorry if my description isn't clear. Any help would be appreciated!

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] resuming updating
parts:
Stan (and NUTS in particular) can be used without adaptation which is probably how you'd want to use it here.  You can specify the stepsize parameter by hand (or adapt it somehow outside of Stan and fix it for each run) and then turn off warmup/adaptation when you run Stan to try to do what you're proposing.  It's likely to work much better than MH assuming you can find reasonable settings for the stepsize parameter.

Cheers,
Marcus
